responses.body:
AI agents for support teams: a practical guide

Support teams answer the same twenty questions every day. An AI agent can draft those answers, but only if it can see your help center and your ticket history.

In this guide we build a triage agent in n8n: it reads a new ticket, searches the knowledge base, and drafts a reply for a human to approve.

Start small. Pick one queue, measure first-response time for two weeks, then expand.

Related posts

Self-hosting n8n on a $5 server

You do not need Kubernetes to run n8n. A small VPS, Docker Compose and a reverse proxy get you a production-ready instance in an afternoon.

We walk through backups, updates and the three environment variables everyone forgets.

If your workflows grow, queue mode is one flag away.

Related posts

Workflow of the month: matching invoices to payments

Finance teams spend hours matching bank lines to invoices. This month's community workflow does it in minutes.

It pulls transactions from the bank API, fuzzy-matches them against open invoices, and flags the leftovers in Slack.

The best part: no code node needed.

Related posts

What is RAG, and when should you use it?

Retrieval-augmented generation lets a model answer from your documents instead of its memory.

Use it when answers must be current or private; skip it when a good prompt is enough.

Here is a five-node RAG starter you can copy.

Related posts

n8n 2.40: faster editor, better errors

Version 2.40 makes the canvas twice as fast on large workflows and rewrites error messages in plain language.

We also added a dry-run mode for webhooks.

Upgrade notes are at the end of this post.
